title: Model Behavioral Canary: cross-region competitive-signal attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: build a lightweight, repeatable 'behavioral canary' and attribution framework that continuously surfaces competitive model changes across regions and signals whether a model substitution or degradation is impacting our customers. Deliverables: 1) Signal taxonomy (latency, token-cost delta, structured-output schema drift, top-n token distribution shift, reranking/QA accuracy delta), 2) Canary harness spec (synthetic prompts, regional routing, per-tenant sampling), 3) Attribution rubric (how to map signal deltas to likely cause: model update, quantization variant, infra/regional degradation, prompt/manifest drift), 4) Dashboard spec and alerting thresholds, 5) Runbook for PM/Eng/Support with recommended mitigations (auto-fallback to pinned variants, customer communication templates). Success criteria: consistent detection of >80% of simulated model-behavior regressions in lab, actionable alerts with suggested mitigation path, low false-positive rate (<10%) when tested against baseline noise workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy documented and reviewed by Research & SRE
Canary harness implemented for hosted and dedicated modes with reproducible runs
Dashboard prototype showing cross-region scorecards and drilldowns
Alerting rules in PagerDuty for high-severity attribution cases
Runbook published in Confluence with playbook steps and communication templates
